title: Popular Made in China HotHands Rechargeable Hand Warmers Recalled Over Fire, Burn Hazard
text:

The recall, announced Oct. 1, covers white-and-orange HotHands rechargeable hand warmers sold in two-packs. The devices can attach magnetically to each other and include a charging cable.
Each warmer contains a built-in lithium-ion battery and has a USB-C charging port. The adjustable-heat units feature LED indicator lights on a hard plastic exterior and include a silicone lanyard.
Consumers can identify the recalled products by model number H163650, which appears on the underside of the warmer with a batch number. The white HotHands logo appears on the product and its packaging.
The recall applies only to electric rechargeable hand warmers bearing the white HotHands logo.
Where Products Were Sold
The recalled warmers were sold from July 2025 through August 2026 for about $30 to $40. They were available at Bass Pro Shops, Meijer, Target, The Home Depot, and other retailers nationwide, as well as online through Amazon.Refund and Disposal
Consumers should immediately stop using the hand warmers and contact Kobayashi for a full refund, according to the commission.To seek a refund, consumers must submit a claim through Kobayashi’s recall webpage and obtain a claim number. They must then write “Recalled” and the claim number on the product with permanent marker and submit a photograph showing the marked warmer, its model number, and the four-digit batch number.
Consumers should dispose of the recalled devices according to applicable state and local hazardous-waste rules.
The devices should not be put in household trash, curbside recycling, general recycling streams, or retail battery-recycling boxes. Recalled lithium-ion batteries require separate disposal because of their elevated fire risk.
saidlithium-ion batteries can overheat, catch fire, or explode when they are damaged or improperly used, charged, or stored. Such fires can produce heat, smoke, toxic gases and explosions.
The association advises consumers to stop using lithium-ion devices that develop unusual odors, excessive heat, popping noises, swelling, or discoloration. It also recommends using only compatible charging equipment, ending charging once a battery is full, and having repairs completed by qualified professionals.
